quests.instruction: Shadow the host's line. Where do the natural breaks fall?
quests.word: Right, so, if you'd like to follow me, I'll show you to your table.
quests.textToSpeak: Right, so, if you'd like to follow me, I'll show you to your table.
options: After every four words, regardless of the meaning
After 'Right' and 'so' as small markers, after 'follow me', then one flowing clause
Only after 'me', with 'Right' and 'so' run into the next clause
quests.correctAnswer: After 'Right' and 'so' as small markers, after 'follow me', then one flowing clause
quests.ipa: /ˈraɪt | ˈsəʊ | ɪf jʊd ˈlaɪk tə ˈfɒləʊ ˈmiː | aɪl ˈʃəʊ jə tə jə ˈteɪbl/
quests.hint: Listen for the discourse words at the very start.
quests.explanation: Markers 'right, so' are light, 'if you'd like to follow me' is the condition, and the main clause runs on.
quests.flowRule: Thought Groups: markers, conditions and main clauses each form their own group.

quests.textToSpeak: The report, which was due on Friday, still hasn't been submitted.

Without any break, in a flat tone
Lower and quicker, bracketed by short breaks

quests.hint: Treat it as extra information whispered in brackets.
quests.explanation: Non-defining clauses are side information, so they sit lower in pitch between short breaks.
quests.flowRule: Parenthetical Thought Groups: side information is spoken faster and lower than the main message.

quests.explanation: A filled pause before the noun is natural when the speaker is searching; pausing elsewhere splits a verb phrase.
